prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, which opened the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep a single-part B022 prize as my preferred configuration. The scientific core is a sequence that is rare in condensed matter: a quantitative prediction in 2011 (Bistritzer and MacDonald) that flat bands appear near a specific twist angle, followed in 2018 by the observation of correlated insulating states and superconductivity at tunable density (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators). The phenomenology has since been reproduced by many laboratories, in several device geometries and in related moire systems, so the existence of the phases is not in dispute; what remains open is the pairing mechanism, and the citation should not claim it. B022 is also the only shortlisted candidate that all eight members ranked, and the eight round-1 files show that the four members who prefer B012 still list B022 as their first or second alternative. That is evidence the committee regards it as scientifically secure enough to defend, and my chair summary recorded that every B022 supporter and every B012 supporter is prepared to move to the other if one specific concern is resolved. Judged as an experimentalist, what persuades me is that the effect was found by measurement in a controllable device, not inferred from a model.
statement.case_against: Three reservations remain and I do not think any of them is trivial. First, maturity: about eight years, with the superconducting mechanism and several correlated states still debated and with sample-to-sample twist-angle disorder. Second, experimental credit: Dean's hBN-encapsulated devices, the first author of the 2018 papers, and the groups of Young, Yacoby, Efetov and Yazdani are outside the three names, and the three-person cap forces a cut. Third, the theory credit is narrower than the headline suggests: as Eriksson points out, the continuum model gives flat bands but does not by itself predict the correlated phases. Against these, B012 has the cleanest two-name attribution and years of independent confirmation, and if the committee judges either the credit gap or the age of the field to be disqualifying I would support B012 without much hesitation.

responses.point: Kroll prefers B012 because the lattice clock is independently confirmed for years, the Katori-Ye credit is short, and the moire field should be allowed to mature; he also asks that a clock citation name the lattice-clock architecture so that ion-clock and comb contributors are not implicitly demoted.
responses.response: I accept that his wording proposal is right and I would back it if B012 prevailed: the citation should name the magic-wavelength lattice architecture and its 10^-18 realisation, and should not say anything about optical clocks in general. Where I still differ is the weight of maturity. Reproduction across independent groups is the test that matters to me, and B022 passes it; the open mechanism is an interpretation question, not a question of whether the discovery is real. I also note that B012's cleaner credit is relative, since by his own and Lindroth's account the ion-clock and national-laboratory groups are outside Katori and Ye as well. The attribution problems differ in kind more than in size.

responses.point: Eriksson cautions that the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model gives flat bands but does not predict the correlated insulators or superconductivity, so the citation must not suggest that theory predicted the correlated phases.
responses.response: I adopt this correction. My round-1 citation was too loose on that point, and the citation above now credits theory only with the prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and credits the experiment alone with the correlated insulating and superconducting states. This also answers part of the chair's question about wording: no mechanism and no claim of predicted phases. I would still say the theory credit is defensible, because the magic angle was a specific, testable number that directed the experiment, but I agree that this is the limit of what it supports.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B022 sixth as premature, given the unresolved superconducting mechanism and variability between samples, and asks whether the redefinition of the second or the passage of time should settle B012 first.
responses.response: I take the prematurity concern as the best argument against my own position and I do not dismiss it. My answer is that his criterion, a settled mechanism, has not been applied to earlier prizes for discoveries whose microscopic explanation came later, and that the evidence the committee needs is reproducibility, which B022 has. Since he has moved his own first place to B012 and no longer presses B038, I would ask him whether the credit problem or the age of the field is the decisive reason, because if it is only age, then a few years would change the answer, and that is a statement about timing, not about merit.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B012 first but accepts that B022 has broader support and a cleaner theory-then-experiment arc, with her reservation being experimental attribution (Cao and co-workers, Dean's group) and the field's youth, and she says B022's broader support could outweigh the clock's cleaner attribution if attribution can be settled within three names.
responses.response: We agree that attribution is the hinge, so I should be explicit about what I can and cannot do. I cannot independently verify the 2018 author record from the materials I am permitted to use at this stage, and I do not want to claim that I have. What I can say is that the prize is for the discovery, the group that led the first reports (Jarillo-Herrero) is the one name the committee has consistently supplied, and Cao as first author, and Dean's devices, are the most serious omission and a consequence of the three-person rule. If she and Kroll believe that omission is large enough to move B022 below B012, I would rather the committee say so openly in the vote than hide it in the citation.

responses.point: Mehlig argues that shared experimental credit is common in modern materials experiments, that the prize can recognise the group leader while the citation names the discovery, and that a lasting-benefit criterion favours a new regime of matter over a measurement platform.
responses.response: I agree with his reasoning on credit and with his wish that the citation say the claim rests on transport and device evidence, not only on the theory prediction. I would qualify the lasting-benefit argument: the committee should not discount B012 as only an instrument, because it also changed what can be tested, and I would not make my case for B022 by diminishing it. My preference rests on breadth of the field opened and on committee-wide support, with B012 as an honest second choice.

uncertainties: Whether the first reports and early follow-up papers (Cao, Dean, Young, Yacoby, Efetov, Yazdani) would, on inspection of the authorship record, make the three-name allocation unacceptable; I could not verify this under the round-2 rules.
Whether eight years is enough maturity given the open pairing mechanism, and whether this alone is a reason to prefer B012 now.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that restricts theory credit to flat bands at a magic angle and does not imply predicted correlated phases.
Whether the pending SI redefinition of the second should be read as evidence for B012; I treat it as supporting evidence at most and not as a criterion.
I found no fair two-part split of B022 and B012 within the three-person limit, so I propose a single part.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile records membership in PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and a background in astroparticle detection, which is field proximity to B013 and, more loosely, B027 and B008, with no documented tie to any credited individual. I have no documented tie to B022, B012 or B018 and no recusal is needed for my preferred configuration. As chair I have tried to treat both leading positions evenly.
